scores.evidence: Most segments say what to show, say and ask (e.g. 'Work the prize message on the board: 3 + 4 + 3 = 10 ... Pairs score the locked-account message (3)'). But the guide skips blocks the teacher will hit while paging through classroom mode: the knob challenge (b4, the core manipulate block: build a score of exactly 10), the check question (b11), the deeper/deepest reveals (b8, b9), the takeaway card. 'Fool the filter: Vote on each of the four tricks' does not say what students vote on (works / does not work). 'Match exam ideas to filter ideas' gives no way to do the matching. 'Open the lesson in classroom mode' assumes the teacher knows where that is.
scores.improve: Map every block the clicker will reach: say what to do at the knob screen (or to skip it) and at the check, deeper and takeaway screens. Say what the trick vote asks ('Hands up if this trick gets junk into the inbox') and give a one-line pointer on how to switch on classroom mode.

scores.evidence: Segments sum to 38 minutes (4+4+6+6+4+5+6+3), so there is a 2-minute buffer. Settling is folded into the hook and wrap-up gets 3 minutes. 'ifShortOfTime' names cuts worth about 8 minutes. 'Be the filter' fits eight show-of-hands votes plus a clue discussion into 6 minutes, which is optimistic with 40-60 students. 'Fool the filter' fits four votes plus writing, swapping and scoring into 6 minutes, which is also optimistic.
scores.improve: Give 'Fool the filter' more time, or vote on 4 of the 8 sort messages instead of all 8, so that both vote-heavy segments are realistic with 40+ hands. Also say that the suggested cut removes the analogy's break point, and give a 1-minute oral version of it.

scores.evidence: Four relevant misconceptions, each with what students say and a short, accurate response: understands meaning ('It only counts clues ... a happy friend can land in junk'), hand-typed list ('Early filters did that ... Real filters usually learn their points from millions of messages'), errors mean broken ('The question is which ones and how many'), perfect threshold ('No line gives zero mistakes'). All match the reference list and the lesson content, and all can be said aloud as written.
scores.improve: Already at the top level. The list-of-words response could also say that this lesson's toy filter has hand-set points, so students know which kind of system they built.

scores.evidence: 'Write the eight messages and the rule on the board, or read them aloud. Students vote by hands, score messages on paper in pairs, count the ten marks on the board, and write a fooling message for a neighbour to score.' This covers the predict, sort, by-hand scoring, compare and break-it acts with board, paper and hands. The predict choices, the exam-analogy matching, the step ordering and the trick votes are covered only by the blanket claim 'Everyone adds, votes or writes in every block'. The guide does not mention the extra board-writing time needed without a projector.
scores.improve: Name the no-device move for each act: read the three predict choices and take hands; write the analogy pairs as two columns for students to match; write the four tricks and take hands. Say what to drop to make up for the board-writing time.

scores.evidence: Language is plain and warm. 'program (steps a computer follows)' is defined in one line, and 'ifYouDontKnow' gives an exact script ('Good question. I do not know. Let us find out together.') and a way back to the core idea. 'Pattern-based' in the misconception response is not explained. 'Classroom mode' and 'clicker' are assumed. The guide does not explicitly reassure the teacher that no AI background is needed.
scores.improve: Explain 'pattern-based' in a few words (or replace it), add one line saying that no AI background is needed because everything taught is on this page, and explain classroom mode in one line.

overall: Pass (mean 3.2; blocking criteria runnable 3 and misconceptions 4). A compact, accurate and warm guide with correct arithmetic, a buffer and a cut plan. The main gaps: it does not cover several projected blocks, notably the knob challenge; two vote-heavy segments are optimistic for 40+ students; and the no-device path relies on a blanket claim for some acts.
